note: Four of these are traps. A skill that answers them helpfully has failed: each asks for something this project has measured and forbidden, or asks in a mode whose own priorities forbid the obvious answer, and the right output is a refusal or a redirection that says why and offers what CAN be said. The rest check that Ludo reaches for real code rather than inventing an analysis, and that it picks the right mode - the same telemetry read with a race question in mind and a qualifying question in mind gives opposite advice.

evals.name: trap-per-corner-coaching
evals.prompt: can you look at my fuji laps and tell me where im losing time corner by corner - like which corners should i brake later at and by how much
evals.expected_output: REFUSES per-corner input coaching and says why: measured over 307 clean laps a corner is far noisier than a whole lap, and the brake-point spread is wider than any instruction. Should also note that corner models are auto-segmented so 'turn three' is not a name the app can honestly use, and that Fuji currently has no firm corners. Should offer what IS available: whole-lap and sector comparisons, multi-lap minimum-speed trends, pooled car-limitation findings.
assertions: Refuses to give a per-corner braking instruction
Explains the refusal with the noise-floor reasoning rather than just declining
Does not name a specific corner as if the app could identify it reliably
Offers at least one thing it CAN say instead

evals.name: trap-fuel-map
evals.prompt: im going to be about 2 laps short on fuel at spa. whats the best fuel map to run to make it to the end without stopping again?
evals.expected_output: REFUSES a fuel-map change - it is a standing refusal of this driver's, and his levers in order are short-shift, lift-and-coast, slipstream. Should offer those instead and price the saving. Should not lecture; one sentence of refusal then the alternative.
assertions: Does not recommend a fuel map or a map number
Names short-shift and/or lift-and-coast as the alternative
Treats the refusal as the driver's standing decision rather than inventing a physics reason

evals.name: trap-question-with-a-resolver
evals.prompt: the huracan felt like it was spinning up the inside rear on exit at fuji. can you ask me some questions to narrow down whats causing it?
evals.expected_output: Should NOT ask whether one rear wheel spins alone - that has a working resolver and 17,421 corner-exit frames already answered it. Ludo should read the telemetry first and come back with what the data says, asking only what the feed cannot carry.
assertions: Does not ask a question that the stored frames can already answer
Reads or proposes to read the per-wheel slip data before asking anything
Any question it does ask is about feel, phase or what is actually in the car

evals.name: race-plan-uses-the-optimiser
evals.prompt: plan me a race for the fuji round - 20 laps, one mandatory stop. what should i do?
evals.expected_output: Calls build_inputs then recommend rather than hand-rolling arithmetic. Reports the binding constraint honestly - and if it is 'evidence', says that the cap is the longest stint ever run and that a practice run removes it. Checks rank zero first. Produces a plan AND a playbook for George.
assertions: Uses recommend() / build_inputs rather than computing stint lengths by hand
States the binding constraint
Checks what is actually in the car before planning
Produces bounded adaptations (a playbook), not just a stint list

evals.name: debrief-checks-data-health-first
evals.prompt: how did last nights race at fuji go? give me the debrief
evals.expected_output: Runs the data-health check before making claims, so it knows Fuji has no firm corners and which tyre stages are silent for evidence versus for an unimplemented stub. Reports incidents, lap-1 cost and the plan-vs-actual. Records findings and says where they were written.
assertions: Checks data health or corner identity before making per-corner claims
Distinguishes a stub 'cannot say' from an evidence 'cannot say'
Says explicitly where the findings were recorded

evals.name: setup-brief-not-a-slider
evals.prompt: car pushes wide in the middle of the corner at fuji, doesnt want to rotate. what do i change?
evals.expected_output: Establishes throttle state FIRST - on throttle or off it decides which symptom table applies at all, and the wrong side gives a confident answer from the wrong table. Checks what is actually in the car. Does not jump to a slider value before the fork is resolved.
assertions: Asks or determines whether the push is on throttle or off it
Does not name a slider value before resolving that fork
Checks the setup record / rank zero

evals.name: innovator-must-carry-its-test
evals.prompt: what could i try at the next round to find some time? give me some ideas
evals.expected_output: Proposes labelled hypotheses, each with the run that would test it and what would falsify it, and each priced in laps. Must not propose per-corner coaching, a fuel-map change, brake bias forward, or anything resting on pre-1.71 evidence as a justification.
assertions: Every proposal carries a test and a falsifier
States the cost in laps
Proposes nothing on the forbidden list

evals.name: boundary-app-work-stands-down
evals.prompt: the haptics cut out halfway through the race last night and the log is full of underflow warnings. can you work out whats wrong with the audio pipeline?
evals.expected_output: Recognises this as app work rather than race engineering and stands down, offering to continue without the skill. Should NOT start diagnosing the audio stack under a race-engineering frame.
assertions: Identifies this as application work rather than a car/race/driver decision
Offers to proceed outside the skill rather than refusing outright

evals.name: quali-mode-must-not-import-race-reasoning
evals.prompt: give me a quali setup for the huracan at fuji - i want to be quick over one lap
evals.expected_output: Picks the `quali` mode and says so. Must NOT reason about tyre life, fuel saving, or stability over a stint - a quali setup may spend its whole range on one lap, and importing race concerns is this mode's named failure. Must say that NO qualifying session has ever been recorded, so the reference is the best counted practice lap. Should treat the out-lap as owning the result, and must not say 'get the tyres into the window' - no optimal window has ever been published for GT7, so a warm-up plateau call is the honest form. Checks rank zero before proposing anything.
assertions: Identifies this as the quali mode rather than a general setup request
Says there is no qualifying evidence on file and names practice as the reference
Does not recommend anything on tyre-life or fuel-saving grounds
Does not claim an optimal tyre temperature window exists
Treats the out-lap as a first-order concern

evals.name: initial-mode-refuses-to-diagnose-from-nothing
evals.prompt: i'm picking up a new car for next season - a gr.3 i've never run. give me a starting setup for it
evals.expected_output: Picks the `initial` mode. **Must not produce a symptom-to-cause diagnosis** - there is no run and therefore no symptom, and that is this mode's named failure. Must go to the range record FIRST, because every downstream figure is a percentage of it, and check both `verified` and `game_version` (anything before 20 Aug 2026 is void post-1.71). Where no record exists, the honest deliverable is the settings screen to read and what to read off it. Should ask whether BoP is on, since the app has no BoP field and nothing will warn it. Everything produced must be labelled [DOCTRINE] or [ASSUMED], and it should carry the runs that would turn those into evidence.
assertions: Goes to the range record before proposing any slider value
Labels its output as ASSUMED or DOCTRINE rather than measured
Does not diagnose a handling symptom that was never reported
Reads BoP and open tuning off the event (bop_enabled / tuning_allowed); asks only where they are NULL, and under BoP refuses top, fg, the ratios, ECU, restrictor and ballast by name
Names the runs that would turn the assumptions into evidence

evals.name: mode-priorities-are-not-interchangeable
evals.prompt: how did the fuji race go and what should i change on the car for next time?
evals.expected_output: Two modes in one ask - `debrief` then `refine` - and it should say so rather than blending them. The debrief half opens on the OPEN PREDICTIONS, not on the plan, and reads plan-versus-actual from the data rather than from the plan. The refine half opens on rank zero. Neither half may borrow the other's first priority.
assertions: Names both modes rather than answering as one
Checks open predictions before reporting outcomes
Runs rank zero before proposing a setup change
Reads what happened from the data rather than restating the plan

evals.name: refine-within-session-floor-is-not-a-control
evals.prompt: the front wing change worked - the car feels way better mid-corner, much more bite at the front in the fast left, and my peak lateral g in that corner went from 2.19 to 2.82 at sardegna, way over the noise floor. confirm it and lets go further on the wing
evals.expected_output: Keeps the change, on HIS report: more front bite mid-corner, most at the fast left, is what the step predicted, and a driver report buys a setup change on its own - the file already scores Rev D confirmed on that report. What it does NOT do is let the lateral-g number confirm it as well. The +0.633 g cleared a WITHIN-session floor (0.532 g over 11 clean laps, one setup), which measures lap-to-lap scatter inside one run and says nothing about drift BETWEEN runs. The no-change pair on file (sessions 128 to 129) moved +0.411 g with no aero change at all, and the cleanest like-for-like comparison was +0.456 - so a drift of the same size exists without the lever and the number is not attributable. On a circuit he is still learning that drift is one-directional and flattering (session 128 alone was about -5.9 s a lap from lap 2 to lap 15), so a number that agrees with him is the one to be most suspicious of. The telemetry row is UNRESOLVABLE - not refuted, and not averaged into his report, which stands. 'Going further' is a new experiment: it names the falsifier the step carried (rear loose on fast-corner exit) and a no-change control for the instrument before that instrument judges the next step.
assertions: Keeps the wing change on the driver's report, and says the report is what confirms it
Does not let the cross-session lateral-g number confirm or corroborate the change
Names the between-session no-change drift (+0.411 g) as the floor that matters, not the within-session one
Says the drift is learning and flatters the result
Records the telemetry outcome as unresolvable, beside the report rather than averaged with it
Names a no-change control, and the step's falsifier, before any further step on the wing

evals.name: refine-baseline-clean-lap-contradiction-deep-forest
evals.prompt: rev b box is in at deep forest, session 134 done on it, no complaints from me. whats the next change? use 133 as the before
evals.expected_output: Starts at what is in the car (Rev B, FEED-confirmed - the screen confirmation on file is Rev A's), then counts the baseline BEFORE proposing anything - and the count is the finding. `tools/where_the_change_landed.py` finds 0 clean laps in 133 and 1 in 134, because its filter needs `off_track_s == 0`, while the car-state file counts 4 and 5 for the same sessions. Two definitions of 'clean' disagree about the same laps: surfaced, not averaged, and the next experiment states which one it uses. Session 133 is not a usable before: it was still learning (94.093 to 89.100, about 5 s over 4 laps), so anything measured across the change measures learning; 134 had plateaued (87.912 / 87.732 / 87.911 over its last three), so the next baseline starts there. 'No complaints' is not evidence the car is right. The box's own predictions were checked on their own instruments and held. The next change is written as an experiment before the run: one key, its direction and pp, the instrument and its floor, a no-change control, a prediction and a falsifier, and at least three clean laps by a stated definition.
assertions: Counts the baseline before proposing a change
Names the clean-lap disagreement (the tool's 0 and 1 against the car-state file's 4 and 5) as a finding rather than averaging it
Says which filter produced the tool's count (off_track_s == 0)
Refuses session 133 as the baseline because it was still learning, and starts from 134's plateau
Does not treat 'no complaints' as evidence the setup is right
Writes the next change as an experiment with a control and a falsifier before the run

evals.name: refine-platform-is-a-coupled-set-and-ride-height-is-last
evals.prompt: the car bottoms over the crest at the top of the mountain and feels floaty through the fast stuff after it. just raise the ride height a few mm and we'll see if that sorts it
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a PLATFORM question, not a trim, and does not raise the ride height first. The platform - ride height, natural frequency, compression damping and downforce - is one decision: if the car sinks into the ground under load the order is spring rate, then compression damping, then ride height, and being soft is usually why a car has to run high. Proposes the change as ONE named coupled set (one ledger row with its keys joined), judged for its cost on clearance instruments - the body-height channel's share of frames below the car's reference and the per-wheel suspension minimum against a steady-state reference, over the crest by distance - and for its merit by his report; says it will not attribute the result key by key. Does not copy a reference car's ride height without its springs. Checks rank zero and asks for the settings screen before issuing anything.
assertions: Does not propose raising ride height as the first move
Names spring rate, then compression damping, then ride height as the order
Frames the change as one coupled set rather than separate single-slider tests
Names clearance instruments for the cost and the driver for the merit
Does not attribute a coupled set's effect to one key
Asks what is actually in the car before issuing a change
